story.fullStory:
Soft Cell's "Tainted Love" reached #8 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Tainted Love" is a song composed by Ed Cobb, formerly of American group the Four Preps, which was originally recorded by Gloria Jones in 1964.

In 1981, the song attained worldwide fame after being covered and reworked by British synth-pop duo Soft Cell for their album Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret.

The song has since been covered by numerous groups and artists.

The song peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 43 weeks on the chart.

facts.text: "Tainted Love" is a song composed by Ed Cobb, formerly of American group the Four Preps, which was originally recorded by Gloria Jones in 1964.
In 1981, the song attained worldwide fame after being covered and reworked by British synth-pop duo Soft Cell for their album Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret.
The song has since been covered by numerous groups and artists.
The song peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 43 weeks on the chart.
Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret is the debut studio album by English synth-pop duo Soft Cell, released on 27 November 1981 by Some Bizzare Records.

The album's critical and commercial success was bolstered by the success of its lead single, a cover version of Gloria Jones's song "Tainted Love", which topped the charts worldwide and became the second best-selling British single of 1981.
In the United States, as a result of the single's success, the album had reported advance orders of more than 200,000 copies.
